statement: A common safety architecture was instantiated across autonomous driving and robotics.
Clean explicit safety filtering was effective in both pilot domains under their respective safety contracts.
Gaussian robustness behavior was directionally consistent across all tested cross-domain comparisons.
Structured-state robustness direction was consistent across driving and robotics.
Positive explicit action recovery was observed in both domains for clipping and Lyapunov filtering.
Lyapunov-specific candidate-selection activation was observed in both domains under action perturbation.
Clean task-preservation direction was consistent across both domains for clipping and Lyapunov.
The same safety thresholds were used across autonomous driving and robotics.
The same trained policy weights transfer directly between driving and robotics.
A universal cross-domain safety controller was demonstrated.
The results establish a formal cross-domain safety guarantee.
Production generalization across physical vehicles and robots was demonstrated.
